slides.title: Describing People and Things
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 6: Describing People and Things. Here you learn how to describe people and things with precise words. You collect words for what somebody is like inside, such as kind, honest, friendly and careless, and words for what things are like outside, such as rough, tough, similar and alive. You compare two people with kinder and busier, you tell true stories in the past simple, and you use could to say what somebody was able to do. Along the way you read about Amal, a new girl who discovers that carrying kindness makes everybody feel welcome. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use describing words (adjectives) to talk about people and things.
Describe your favourite person and say what makes them special.
Compare two people or things, using words like kinder and rougher than.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use describing words (adjectives) to talk about people and things. You will also describe your favourite person and say what makes them special. You will also compare two people or things, using words like kinder and rougher than. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: kind, friendly, honest, kindness, care, busy. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes My Cousin Noah and Two Roads. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: The Past Simple Tense
bullets: We use the past simple to talk about things that already happened. It helps us tell stories and describe what people did, like Nora, who helped the boy...
slides.narration: The first language focus is The Past Simple Tense. We use the past simple to talk about things that already happened. It helps us tell stories and describe what people did, like Nora, who helped the boy who fell. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1 — A Description of a Person
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Describe Your Favourite Person. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
